Foodwise: Chongqing
programs.desc: Welcome to Chongqing, China's largest city. Located in the country's southwest, it straddles two mighty rivers and is famed for its extraordinary skyline, with high-rises mushrooming out of the hills and vertigo-inducing bridges.But Tianran He and Angela Fu are here for the food: From xiaomian noodles and Jianghu cuisine to the city's most famous dish: Chongqing hotpot, our hosts take on the spicy, numbing and scintillating aromas of Chongqing cuisine. We promise you: Chongqing will electrify your senses and tantalise your taste buds.

programs.title: A Bite of Xinjiang Ep.5
programs.desc: This is a documentary that comprehensively showcases Xinjiang in all its diversity. Exploring cuisine, landscapes, and folk culture, it shows how diverse ethnic groups drive economic growth, social stability, cultural prosperity, and national unity through diligence and wisdom.

programs.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan
programs.desc: In Episode 5, Kleber travels to Shanxi, the birthplace of Xingyi Quan. He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan's noodle shops to Pingyao's ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan's deep links to Shanxi's merchant culture and history. Master Cao breaks down the core principles of the "Five Elements and Twelve Forms", and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan's philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential. Set against ancient sites such as Yongle Palace, this episode shows how true inner strength is like traditional timber architecture: stable, balanced, and built from within.

programs.title: China Bound: Xiamen
programs.desc: What's it like in one of China's happiest cities? Tianran is in sunny Xiamen on China's southeast coast, visiting the city's famous "island of music" and sampling local delicacies like shark meatballs, shacha noodles and fish in "soy sauce water". He'll discover former fishing villages turned hipster havens, drink tea with locals beneath traditional tenement buildings, and visit a student enclave brimming with creative startup energy.

programs.title: Nanjing Yunjin Brocade: A Traditional Chinese Silk Craft
programs.desc: Nanjing's Yunjin Brocade silk handicraft tradition dates back over 1,600 years, and is famous for its exquisite materials, meticulous weaving, and vibrant, splendid patterns. Its core technique is executed manually by two artisans working above and below complex, large-scale looms. Using materials such as silk floss, gold thread, and peacock feather threads, they create luxurious fabrics like imperial dragon robes.

programs.title: Diabolo
programs.desc: In China, the diabolo has a history of over 600 years. From the earliest uniaxial design, it developed to have a double axis. With time, it came to be made in various shapes and from various materials. And its popularity began to spread around the world. In the hands of an expert, a diabolo can create a truly mesmerizing spectacle. So, let's hear from a professional about the various tricks of his trade.

programs.title: China Bound: Tianjin
programs.desc: Tianran He explores the vibrant port city of Tianjin. Strolling through its historic quarters, he discovers how old buildings are being preserved and revitalized, and savors the rich flavors of authentic Tianjin cuisine. To work off the calories, he joins energetic retirees for a morning workout in the park, then takes in the lively nightlife along the banks of the Haihe River. From folk handicrafts on Ancient Culture Street to the National Maritime Museum and an aircraft carrier theme park, Tianran discovers that Tianjin is a truly multifacted city.

programs.title: Yuxian, a living legacy of ancient architecture and paper-cutting
programs.desc: Yuxian County in Zhangjiakou, north China's Hebei Province is home to numerous national-level cultural heritage sites. The Yuhuang Pavilion, constructed in the Ming Dynasty (1368-1644), once served as a frontier defense structure and later served as an architectural reference for the hit game Black Myth: Wukong. Meanwhile, Yuxian paper-cutting, which originated as window decorations for rural homes, has evolved for over a century into a distinctive form of cultural expression that has reached audiences around the world. CGTN host Julian Waghann and Mexican traveler Juan Carlos Cheang Guzman toured Yuxian, discovering the stories behind its ancient architecture and learning the art of paper-cutting. As local craftspeople and communities keep these traditions alive, Yuxian shows how ancient culture can continue to evolve, connect with new generations and reach the world in new ways.

programs.title: Kung Fu Wise II-6 Shandong Mantis Style
programs.desc: The final episode traces the cross-ocean transmission of Shandong Mantis Style. In the mountains of northern Italy, host Kleber visits Dante Basili, a veteran Italian practitioner in his sixties, who recounts travelling to China 36 years ago to learn Mantis Style and returning home to teach Chinese martial arts ever since. Kleber then heads to Shandong to meet Yu Bo and Yu Tao, sons of Mantis Style grandmaster Yu Hai. He witnesses a traditional apprenticeship ceremony and explores the style's fighting essence: adopting its spirit rather than merely copying its form. The episode shows how Mantis Style has taken root and flourished in different cultural settings. Ultimately, this journey across Europe and Asia suggests that transmission is not only about techniques, but also about dialogue across time and distance, and a shared resonance of spirit between cultures.

programs.title: China Bound: Suzhou
programs.desc: In this episode, Tianran He visits Suzhou, a historic city in eastern China famously admired by Marco Polo. Crisscrossed by canals, Suzhou is renowned for its exquisite gardens, where ancient scholars recreated nature's beauty within their own homes. Tianran discovers a city of refined tastes, where even a bowl of breakfast noodles comes with unspoken etiquette, locals insist on only in-season produce, and foodies eagerly await the arrival of prized hairy crabs.

programs.title: Miao Silverware: A Shining Epic
programs.desc: In this episode, we explore the fascinating world of the silver-working art of the Miao ethnic group. Join us, and hear the stories and see the works of four remarkable individuals. From a national-level inheritor who is preserving the traditional craft, to an artist infusing personal flair into his designs; from a female silversmith imbuing her work with feminine warmth, to a young artisan inspiring a new generation, we investigate the rich heritage, cultural significance, and evolving potential of Miao silverware.

programs.title: Crunch and Munch in Macao Ep.1
Navigating the Hills of Chongqing
programs.desc: This episode explores the transportation ingenuity of Chongqing, the Fog City. Surrounded by mountains and rivers, this megacity solves topographic challenges with the Yangtze River Cableway, Asia's second-longest escalator, and a train passing through a building. From the dock culture at the confluence of two rivers to a logistics hub linking China and Europe, witness its transformation from an inland town to an economic center via the Go West policy.

programs.title: China's Extraordinary Hotels 1 - From Relic to Resort
programs.desc: The first episode of the Hotel Series introduces three hotels reconstructed from ancient buildings , each of the hotels has its unique stunning style: 1. Yingui Boutique Hotel reconstructed from ancient buildings with traditional Bai ethnic minority style in Kunming, Yunnan; 2. Imperial Guard Boutique Hotel reconstructed from Anhui Huangshan Huipai architecture; 3. Yellow River Suji Hotel Group in Shapotou, Zhongwei, Ningxia. This episode explores not only their surrounding landscapes, design concepts, architectural styles and interior furnishings, but also the distinctive natural scenery and profound local cultural features of each region.

programs.desc: The high elevation and abundant sunshine of North China's Zhangbei county makes it a center of off-season fresh produce. Here, sunshine is converted into clean energy, while cutting-edge agricultural technology is integrated into every stage of farming, from seedling cultivation to harvest. We visit a village that is exploring new applications for its excess solar power, pick some indoor-grown watermelons, and enjoy a lively evening around a bonfire.

programs.title: Solar-powered farmlands shape new rural vistas
Foodwise: Veggie Beijing
programs.desc: Beijing is a 3000-year old metropolis home to a dizzying array of culinary traditions, not least of which is vegetarian cuisine. For Beijingers, eating vegetarian is the best way to welcome spring. In this episode, Tianran and Angela take up the challenge: From simple home cooking utilizing spring flowers and leaves, to the extravagant mock-meat masterpieces of imperial cuisine, and international dishes well-known to the vegetarian community, our hosts discover a plethora of plant-based options to be found amongst the historic alleys and skyscrapers of China's capital.

programs.title: In Search of Shunde Ep.1
programs.desc: A Bite of Shunde tells the stories of Shunde locals through food, showcasing this city's heritage and present-day life. It looks at the craftsmanship Shunde people apply in the kitchen and beyond, and the dedicated, artisan mentality behind their renowned culinary culture. Through their attitude toward a simple home-cooked meal, we get insights into their values and way of life.

programs.desc: Feast on the stories behind Macao's iconic dishes and its people - One Country, Two Systems, endless flavors.

programs.title: Yangliuqing New Year Painting Art
programs.desc: On May 20, 2006, Yangliuqing New Year Paintings were named as part of China's national intangible cultural heritage. The New Year painting tradition can be traced back many centuries, to the Ming Dynasty and beyond, reaching the height of its popularity in the Qing Dynasty. There are no restrictions on the themes of the paintings, and there is no blessing they cannot convey. Yangliuqing New Year Paintings are loved all over the country for their beautiful details and vivid colors - but most of all, for the good wishes they impart to anyone who sees them.
